- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.40) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast peak at 1–2% above true peak.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model underreacts; increase forecast slope slightly to match sentiment momentum.
- Model consistently overpredicts 30-day horizon by 1–3% in early summer; apply 1.5–2% downward bias for 30d forecasts.
- If sentiment history shows repeated small negative swings, model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.0% to forecast to compensate for delayed reaction.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model often overestimates mean; apply 1–2% mean reversion correction toward recent 7-day average.
